Split cp:3 fans out to output (0) and hidden 290; one copy per consuming annotation (function-preserving).
Split trestbps fans out to output (0) and hidden 290; one copy per consuming annotation (function-preserving).

Split thal:7 fans out to output (0) and hidden 204; one copy per consuming annotation (function-preserving).

Split hidden gate 204: it reads out both to the output (0) and into gate 290, which belong to different branches of the annotation hierarchy (root vs ischaemia_pathway). The composition validator only treats direct-child nodes as internal, so a single 204 inside a grandchild leaf cannot feed the root output. Copies are bit-identical (function-preserving).

params.name: st_ischaemia_gate_output

payload.interpretation: one-sided ischaemia-evidence detector dominated by ST depression (oldpeak); all weights positive so monotone increasing in each input

records.narrative: Closed form of a single ReLU gate over three inputs; oldpeak weight is 2.3x/2.7x the others.
Genuine gate on training data: hard-zero for 52% of patients, active for 48%. Mean |grad| ranks oldpeak >> thal:7 > restecg:0; oldpeak alone correlates 0.88 with the gate output.

params.hypothesis: Hidden gate 204 = ReLU(2.554*oldpeak + 1.133*thal:7 + 0.937*restecg:0 + 0.276): a one-sided ischaemia-evidence detector that switches on for patients with exercise-induced ST depression and/or a reversible thallium defect, normal resting ECG adding a little. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): hard-zero for 52%, active for 48%; mean |grad| oldpeak 1.23 > thal:7 0.55 > restecg:0 0.45; oldpeak alone correlates 0.88 with the gate. This is the output-facing copy 204_a (bit-identical to 204_b); it reads out directly to the output with +0.117, raising predicted risk.

params.name: thal6_linear_passthrough

payload.simplified_on_data: 2116 = 1.003 thal:6 + 2.165 (both ReLUs always active since thal:6 >= -0.257)

records.narrative: Closed form reduces to an affine map over the data domain; the two ReLUs never clip.
Both nodes are 100% active on training data and 2116 is perfectly linear in thal:6 (r = 1.000). The chain is a linear pass-through whose downstream weight (-0.013) makes it practically inert.

params.hypothesis: Serial chain thal:6 -> 3671 -> 2116: 3671 = ReLU(1.000*thal:6 + 2.123), 2116 = ReLU(1.003*3671 + 0.036). Since thal:6 >= -0.257 on the data both ReLUs are always active (100% on train), so 2116 = 1.003*thal:6 + 2.165 exactly (r = 1.000 on train). It feeds gate 290 with weight -0.013, contributing -0.013*thal:6 - 0.029 to its pre-activation: an always-on affine relay that is functionally a vestige.

payload.readout: logit += 0.135*290 + 0.165*1834 + 0.097*1987 (204_a, the other copy of the ischaemia gate, adds 0.117*204 via the root)
payload.slope_of_logit_in_290: 0.135 baseline; +0.155 extra when 1834 on; -0.154 when 1987 on (age gate cancels the direct readout)

records.narrative: Closed form of the composed pathway; 290 is a serial composition over the child gate, and 1834/1987 are readouts of 290 that respectively amplify strong ischaemia evidence and switch off the age term.

payload.tool_note: composition-level function evaluation (sensitivity/line by annotation_id) ignores child subgraphs, so node_id evaluations were used

records.narrative: Empirics agree with the formula: 1834 fires only in the regime where both 204 and 290 are on (26% of patients, 78% of them diseased) - an amplifier for strong ischaemia evidence. 1987 is on for 64% of patients with 290 quiet but only 13% when 290 is active, confirming that age acts as a fallback risk signal that the ischaemia pathway switches off. 290 is opened by 204 in 100/135 of its active cases; 35 cases open it from low resting BP alone and these patients have low predicted risk (mean 0.13).

params.hypothesis: Serial composition of the ischaemia gate into a BP-adjusted gate and its readouts. (1) Gate 290 = ReLU(1.088*st_ischaemia_gate_bp - 0.817*trestbps + 0.151*cp:2 + 0.017*cp:3 + 0.046*thal:6 - 0.013*thal6_linear_passthrough - 0.485): it passes on the ischaemia evidence of 204_b, offset downward by resting blood pressure (high-BP patients need more ST-depression evidence to open it). (2) 1834 = ReLU(0.941*290 - 1.672): high-threshold amplifier, fires only when 290 > 1.78, making the pathway convex. (3) 1987 = ReLU(0.880*age - 1.585*290 + 0.179): an age term switched OFF by the gate, so age adds risk only for patients in whom 290 is quiet. Output contribution 0.135*290 + 0.165*1834 + 0.097*1987. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 290 active 56% (100/135 of its active cases have 204 on; 35 open from low BP alone, mean predicted risk 0.13); 1834 active 26%, only when 204 and 290 are both on, and 78% of those patients are diseased; 1987 active in 64% of patients with 290 quiet vs 13% with 290 active. The thal:6 chain is functionally inert. Interpretation: the network has exactly one nonlinear mechanism - an ischaemia pathway that amplifies strong ST-depression/defect evidence and uses age as a fallback signal when that evidence is absent.

params.name: heart_disease_logit

payload.function_preserved_check: train AUC/acc/MSE identical before and after all splits

records.narrative: Complete structural and compositional coverage with 10 function-preserving splits; explained network computes the same function as the evolved one.

payload.method: local recomputation of logit decomposition z = linear core + sum(readout weight * node activation); verified sigmoid(z) equals model output to 2e-16; readouts removed without re-fitting

records.narrative: The linear core carries most of the signal; the nonlinear ischaemia machinery adds ~+0.01 train AUC. Test split not inspected (protocol).
Top drivers ca, sex:0, slope:1 are all direct linear-core edges; oldpeak (gate-only input) ranks 7th.

records.narrative: Closed-form root: an 18-term linear logit plus four additive nonlinear readouts from the two children.

params.hypothesis: Root: logit z = -0.496 + LINEAR CORE + 0.117*st_ischaemia_gate_output + ischaemia_pathway readouts (0.135*290 + 0.165*1834 + 0.097*1987); prediction = sigmoid(z) (the genome output node is ReLU but the evaluator overrides it with sigmoid for binary classification, so it is a logistic score). LINEAR CORE (18 direct input->output edges, z-scored inputs): ca +1.51, sex:0 -1.08, slope:1 -0.90, chol +0.53, cp:1 -0.53, trestbps +0.49, cp:3 -0.47, thal:3 -0.43, exang:1 +0.43, slope:3 -0.41, thal:6 -0.38, cp:4 +0.33, fbs:0 +0.28, thalach -0.25, restecg:0 -0.18, exang:0 +0.15, age +0.11, thal:7 -0.07. Signs match cardiology: more fluoroscopy-coloured vessels, male sex, high cholesterol/BP, exertional angina and asymptomatic chest pain raise risk; upsloping ST (slope:1), normal thallium (thal:3), typical/non-anginal pain and high max heart rate lower it. 6 inputs are unused (sex:1, fbs:1, restecg:1, restecg:2, slope:2, thal:4 - mostly redundant one-hot complements or rare categories). COMPOSITION: purely additive in the logit - the two children add to the linear core. Child 1 (st_ischaemia_gate_output) adds a ReLU ischaemia score (oldpeak, thal:7, restecg:0); child 2 (ischaemia_pathway) adds a BP-adjusted, convexly amplified version of the same score, plus an age term that is active only when the score is quiet. oldpeak and thal:7 influence the output ONLY through these gates (oldpeak has no direct edge). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): full model AUC 0.942 / acc 0.876; linear core alone AUC 0.932 (nonlinear parts add +0.010 train AUC); logit SD of linear core 3.18 vs 0.78 for all nonlinear readouts combined. Removing individual readouts: 290 -0.002, 1834 -0.0016, 204_a -0.0016, 1987 -0.0007, whole pathway -0.0055 AUC. Whole-model SHAP (prob scale): ca 0.139, sex:0 0.105, slope:1 0.099, thal:3 0.045, cp:3 0.041, exang:1 0.039, oldpeak 0.038, chol 0.033, cp:4 0.032. The model is essentially a logistic regression with one small nonlinear ischaemia correction.
